about: The curated reference set for this repo's motion language. Every entry is something already published that a ListeningKit scene borrows an idea from. `vendor: true` entries are pulled into docs/references/vendor/ by `npm run refs -- pull`, with provenance, so they can be read offline and by an agent without network. Nothing here is a runtime dependency: scenes are built from src/ and never import vendored files.
how: npm run refs -- list                      show this manifest
npm run refs -- pull [id|--all]           fetch vendored files via the GitHub API into docs/references/vendor/<id>/
npm run refs -- search "<terms>" [repo]   code search across the allowed repos (gh api search/code)
npm run refs -- read <repo> <path>        print one file from a repo, raw
npm run refs -- tree <repo> [prefix]      list a repo's files

entries.why: A camera that follows the content instead of the content moving: every pose is FITTED to the measured box of what is on screen, on a hand-solved cubic bezier.
takeaways: fit each camera pose to a MEASURED bounding box, never a typed coordinate
cubic-bezier ease solved in-file (Newton, bisection fallback): deterministic, any overshoot you like
one shared amount tweened per move, each element carries its own share (radial smear)
entries.notTaken: its word-by-word text layout: the subtitles stay normal bottom captions (matt, 2026-10-03)

entries.why: A finite, seek-safe exposure flash used to hide a cut.
takeaways: light layers with finite duration, no looping CSS
the cut happens at the peak, not before or after it
entries.usedBy: src/build-beats.mjs  the .flash layer and the seam timeline

entries.why: A card stack at different depths under a camera rig: the parallax idea behind the depth set.
takeaways: perspective on a stable parent, preserve-3d on the world, z per layer
the camera is the only thing that moves the layers relative to each other

entries.why: Card tilt with depth layers: how a flat card gets a tilt that reads as a surface.
takeaways: rotationX/Y small (<= 10deg), perspective from the parent
inner layers at their own z

entries.why: A badge that pops in from a visible near-rest scale, overshoots once and settles.
takeaways: start from a visible scale (not 0) for the card itself
one overshoot, then settle

entries.why: A card with a scripted cursor spotlight: a pointer that is part of the choreography, not an overlay.
takeaways: the cursor's path is authored data, evaluated from time
the element reacts to the pointer arriving

entries.why: Dynamic zoom, slide and 3D tilt-pan helpers for any wrapper, with cubic-easing defaults.
takeaways: move the WRAPPER, never the media
zoom and tilt are one move

entries.why: Cards slide-settle into a stack on cues, newest on top: entrances driven by cue times rather than fixed offsets.
takeaways: entrance times come from a cue list
one card is grown slightly to carry focus

entries.why: A single hit: impact flash, micro scale-pulse on the subject, immediate decay.
takeaways: a hit is a flash plus a pulse plus a fast decay, never a held glow

entries.why: The depth-group grammar: groups at different distances so camera moves pull them apart by parallax; focus follows depth; a whip-in that never lands.
takeaways: every group gets its own depth; near is bigger, far is smaller and slower
the camera creep keeps a held shot alive
rules for keeping everything inside the frame (frame-bounds check)
entries.notTaken: text in 3D, matte and talking-head plate: this series has no speaker and keeps normal subtitles

entries.why: The framework's own guidance on easing and stagger, including that back.out(1.7) is a deliberate playful register.
takeaways: power3.out is the house entrance
overshoot is a decision, and here it is the decision: the series is cartoon-cinematic

entries.why: Curated Opus 5.5 videos with originals and prompts; the implementation guide for the beat-synced UI morph loop is the source of 'a visible cursor must cause every click'.
takeaways: a visible cursor causes every click and drag
ban dead time
render one still per beat before the full pass

entries.why: The largest collection of viral Opus 5.5 videos with prompts. Search it by phrase for motion-heavy product work.
A 'Product demos & ads' section with original posts and many full prompts.
Real HyperFrames compositions with the exact prompts: useful as worked examples of the composition contract.
